rv.q: The note of hope in this play, and it is rightly centered in this unpretentious and powerful production, is that the human spirit is far harder to defeat than the body.
Their struggle — for survival, for sanity, for keeping their dignity and holding fast to the principles that got them arrested — is compelling in Randle-Bent’s furiously paced production.
The Island is a riveting, philosophically sophisticated play that is a must-see for fans of meaty theater.
Please see “The Island” at Court Theatre, it’s as important now as it was 50 years ago.
The Island was a painful reminder of the abuse blacks endured during Apartheid and how the power of theater can liberate and provoke change.
The transformation that takes place is phenomenal.
And last night, they showed how grand they can be.
